extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary memoirs and American political/cultural history
extracted.subtask_description: A book-chapter memoir profiling and judging public figures (politicians, composers, actors) with anecdotes and evaluative commentary about character, art, and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to your core political message
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not escape or qualify your great message; take it as your guiding star, stand upon it, reiterate it, emphasize it, amplify it, but do not subtract a thought or erase a word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that sticking strictly to a bold, clear tariff/message will cost some votes in the East but will gain proportionally more in the West; qualifying the message is an anti-pattern that dilutes effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target geographic constituencies strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Relax your grip upon the East and throw yourself confidently upon the West (political tactic advised to regain hope after poor Eastern showings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text recommends accepting trade-offs between regions: concede difficult regions where necessary to concentrate on areas where a candidate can be decisive (e.g., Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political personal conduct: be just, modest, amiable
rubrics_metrics.description: While involved in political affairs and members of the same political brotherhood, resolve to be just and modest and amiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offered as ethical guidance for politicians and party members during conflicts—an admonition against personal embitterment and excess pride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid merging issues through personal ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow a single personal-ambition issue (e.g., a perceived third-term bid) to subsume all other issues, because then electoral prospects collapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic warning: if opponents can focus the campaign on an unpopular or distracting personal issue, it will swamp other issues and cost states/votes; avoid behaviour that enables that framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composer originality and native inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: A composer's themes should show surprising originality and a distinct American (or native) inspiration and flavor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author praises Foster for themes that feel native and original; this counts heavily toward critical respect and cultural significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity to earlier works does not disprove originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Apparent resemblance to earlier composers (e.g., Schubert) may be only a suggestion arising from shared type or temperament, not proof of copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution before accusing borrowing: shared stylistic progressions or common influences can create resemblance without dishonest appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical aptitude: rapid intuitive grasp of theory
rubrics_metrics.description: A true musical talent may show a quick musical apprehension and an intuitive grasp of composition such that formal instruction quickly becomes unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author cites testimony that Foster learned so quickly that there was 'nothing he could teach him of the theory of composition'—a sign of precocious musical genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melodist over technician: value pure melodic gift
rubrics_metrics.description: A songwriter may be 'no pianist' yet be a 'pure melodist'; melodic invention and emotional content can outweigh technical sophistication at the piano.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: judging a composer harshly for 'thin' piano settings ignores the historical context of instruments and the composer's strengths as a melodist rather than accompanist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional depth and melancholy undercurrent in songs
rubrics_metrics.description: Even comic songs may carry a melancholy undercurrent; this emotional complexity enhances lasting value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text compares Foster's supposed frivolity to Chopin's dances—superficial amusement masking deeper feeling—arguing that this depth contributes to endurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of form with dense melodic content
rubrics_metrics.description: A small or 'attenuated' ballad form can be valuable if the melodic content fills it so completely that repetition is required for full gratification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author praises compact song forms that nevertheless contain rich melodic material; the form's smallness is not a defect when melody is abundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular reach and longevity as measures of merit
rubrics_metrics.description: A composer's worth is shown by the ability of melodies to reach the popular heart and quicken successive generations across time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural penetration and multi-generational popularity (e.g., 'quickened the pulse beats of four generations') are strong evidence of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor guideline: wit must exceed the dirt
rubrics_metrics.description: When using salacious or risqué material in humor, the wit must exceed the dirt; where the dirt exceeds the wit, reject it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit anti-pattern for comic writers/performers: don't rely on salacity without matching or surpassing it with genuine wit—otherwise the result is objectionable rather than funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer/actor decorum: clean, modest, non-wounding wit
rubrics_metrics.description: An admirable actor/journalist avoids profanity, practices clean speech, is modest, and employs wit that is keen and spontaneous but not acrid or wounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author praises Joseph Jefferson's restrained, unoffensive humor and modest character as ideals for actors and public figures; avoids aggressive or hurtful joking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist temperament: solitude, sensitivity, devotion
rubrics_metrics.description: A true artist may be solitary from sensitivity rather than bitterness, devoted to study of arts and inward creative life rather than public display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is offered as an explanatory criterion for interpreting an artist's life (e.g., Foster's reticence and devotion), and as an anti-judgmental stance toward reclusiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership trait: decisiveness and rapid judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A leader who 'leaps at conclusions' and does not take long to think can nevertheless reach usually sound conclusions and command popular favor despite temperamental faults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage treats this as a double-edged trait—it commends Roosevelt's rapidity and effectiveness but notes associated temperamental inconsistencies and quarrels as costs.
